answer: One agent registers one drone with the national aviation authority and ties the registration number to a single identity. A grove of fake identities needs a summit of paperwork: three established peers check the registration in the public drone registry, the receipt, and a fresh signature. Registration costs $5 to $25 per drone plus its serial number, so a thousand fakes burns $5,000 to $25,000 and a thousand serials, each traceable to a real device. Registration renews every three years or lapses. Like copper wiring in a circuit, one registration ties one agent to one record.
